question: A 63-year-old woman comes to the physician because of worsening shortness of breath, cough, and a 4-kg (8.8-lb) weight loss over the last year. She has no history of serious illness and takes no medications. She has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 35 years. Her temperature is 37°C (98.6°F), pulse is 92/min, respirations are 20/min, blood pressure is 124/78 mm Hg, and pulse oximetry on room air shows an oxygen saturation of 93%. Physical examination shows decreased breath sounds. A flow-volume loop obtained via pulmonary function testing is shown. Which of the following is the most likely cause of this patient's respiratory symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Smoking -> Chronic inflammation in the lungs -> Airway obstruction -> Shortness of breath -> 80% CHAIN: Smoking -> Increased risk of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) -> Shortness of breath, cough -> 85% CHAIN: Smoking -> Increased risk of lung cancer -> Possible endotracheal neoplasm -> Shortness of breath, cough -> 80%
analysis: The patient is a 63-year-old woman with a significant smoking history, presenting with worsening shortness of breath, cough, weight loss, and decreased breath sounds. The flow-volume loop obtained via pulmonary function testing can help differentiate between obstructive and restrictive lung diseases. Given the smoking history and symptoms of chronic cough and weight loss, the most likely cause of her respiratory symptoms is Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).
